newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada sees talks resuming with CAW.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada sees talks resuming with CAW.

text.p: Air Canada expects talks with a union representing 3,500 of its customer sales and ticket agents to resume before any strike date set by the union, the carrier's president and chief executive Lamarr Durrett told reporters on Wednesday.

Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) local 2213 said on Wednesday that a conciliation meeting with the carrier on the contract talks ended Tuesday without progress. The CAW said it may put the Air Canada agents in a strike position before Christmas.
"We do expect the negotiations to recommence before any legal strike date," Durrett said in a conference phone call.
Durrett said the CAW union strike date could be set for December 15.

"It is my belief that as long as both sides are talking, reasonable people will be able to work through these issues, and we are going to remain optimistic that we are going to be able to get that done," he said.

Durrett said the membership of a Canadian Union of Public Employees (CUPE) representing some of the carrier's flight attendants recently voted 65 percent to reject a tentative agreement between Air Canada and the union leadership on a contract offer.
At March 31, CUPE represented 3,265 flight attendants at Air Canada. Durrett said once CUPE seeks some form of unified mandate from its members, contract talks would likely continue.

Air Canada chief financial officer Robert Peterson said the carrier had reduced its debt reduction target for the fourth quarter to C$250 million from about C$500 million forecast earlier, mainly because of two factors.
The company had expected a transaction involving the sale and leaseback of part of its fleet of 35 DC-9 aircraft to be concluded in the fourth quarter.
But the deal was put off when U.S. regulators grounded potential buyer ValuJet Inc in June after a fatal plane crash in May.
"That was about C$100 million that we won't be getting in, it doesn't look like this year," Peterson said.
ValuJet is flying again and is gradually rebuilding its flight schedule. The sale to Valujet of some of Air Canada's DC-9 fleet, which it is retiring, could come in the new year.
Peterson He said Air Canada had also expected to sell the balance of its shares in Continental Airlines Inc, but that transaction will likely be put off until next year.
Peterson said, however, that plans to proceed in the fourth quarter with a refinancing of four Airbus A-320 aircraft and seven Canadair Regional Jets it owns.
"That refinancing is going well. That amounts to almost C$300 million and proceeds will go to debt reduction," he said.
That means debt reduction that does not happen in the current fourth quarter will likely occur before the end of next year, he said.
